transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hello, is that Priya Ramaswamy-Holt?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, speaking.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hi Priya, it's Dr Whitlock, calling back from the surgery. Is now a good time to talk, and are you somewhere private?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm at home. That's fine.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Can you confirm your date of birth for me?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Second of November, ninety-seven.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Thank you. The receptionist said you're having some waterworks problems?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It's burning when I wee, and I keep needing to go, like every half an hour.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How long has this been going on?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Since yesterday. Sorry, no, since Saturday. So three days now.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay, three days. Have you noticed any blood in your urine?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Maybe a little pinkish this morning.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any pain in your back or sides, just under your ribs?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any fever, shivers or shakes?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I don't think so. I feel okay in myself.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any feeling sick, or vomiting?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any unusual vaginal discharge, or itching?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Have you had anything like this before?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Once, about two years ago. I had antibiotics and it cleared up.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Do you remember which antibiotic?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, sorry.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: That's fine. Is there any chance you could be pregnant?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't think so. Well... actually my period is about a week late. But that happens sometimes.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay. Have you done a pregnancy test?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, not yet.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: That's useful to know, because it affects which antibiotics are safe. Do you take any regular medicines?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Just vitamin D in the winter.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any allergies to medicines?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, none.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any problems with your kidneys?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay. I can't examine you over the phone, but you're speaking comfortably in full sentences and you sound well. From what you've told me, this sounds like a urine infection in the bladder, a cystitis.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought so.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I'm going to prescribe nitrofurantoin. It's 100 milligrams, the modified-release capsules, twice a day for seven days. That's a good choice for bladder infections and it's suitable even if you do turn out to be pregnant, early on.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Because your period's late, I'd like you to do a pregnancy test today, and please drop a urine sample into the surgery before you start the antibiotics, so we can send it to the lab.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Great. And please ring us back tomorrow with the pregnancy test result. If it's positive, we'll need to see you, and the treatment plan changes a bit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Drink plenty of fluids, and you can take paracetamol for the discomfort.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Can I take ibuprofen?

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I'd stick to paracetamol for now, until you know whether you're pregnant.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: If you develop pain in your back or side, a fever, shivering, or vomiting, that could mean the infection has spread to the kidneys. In that case call us straight away, or 111 if we're closed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: And if you're not starting to feel better within 48 hours of starting the antibiotics, or you're getting worse, call us back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: You're welcome. Take care, Priya.

reference_note.presenting_complaint: Dysuria and urinary frequency for 3 days.
reference_note.history: Dysuria and frequency (about every 30 minutes) since Saturday. Possible pink-tinged urine this morning. No loin pain, fever, rigors, nausea or vomiting. No vaginal discharge or itch. One previous UTI two years ago, treated with antibiotics (agent unknown). Period approximately one week late; no pregnancy test yet. No known renal disease.
reference_note.medications_allergies: Vitamin D (winter). No known drug allergies.
reference_note.examination: Telephone consultation; not examined. Speaking in full sentences and sounds well.
reference_note.impression: Lower urinary tract infection (cystitis). Possible early pregnancy, to be excluded.
reference_note.plan: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg modified-release twice daily for 7 days. Pregnancy test today. Urine sample for culture before starting antibiotics. Call back tomorrow with pregnancy test result; if positive, face-to-face review and plan revised. Fluids and paracetamol; avoid ibuprofen until pregnancy excluded.
reference_note.safety_netting: Call the practice (or 111 out of hours) immediately if loin pain, fever, rigors or vomiting. Call back if not improving within 48 hours of starting antibiotics or worsening.
